documents.title: Linden Search LS-417 Early-Career Engineer Retrieval Platform
documents.text: The Retrieval Platform group builds the shared systems that turn customer documents into queryable indexes. Early-career engineers pair with experienced engineers on ingestion diagnostics, indexing jobs, service interfaces and evaluation tooling. Recent projects include understanding the cost of compacting small index segments and comparing query results across new index versions. Work includes writing tests, inspecting operational metrics and documenting decisions for colleagues who use the platform. Candidates should be comfortable programming backend services, reasoning about data structures and communicating tradeoffs. Experience with databases, retrieval experiments or storage projects can provide useful foundations; expertise in every listed system is not expected. The role is based in the United States and includes collaboration with evaluation and storage engineers. Applications open as of November 7. Requisition LS-417.

documents.title: Retrieval infrastructure charter
documents.text: Retrieval Infrastructure maintains indexing, segment storage and evaluation tooling used by several product teams. Priya Iyer focuses on evaluation instrumentation and comparing query quality across index releases. Jordan Wells focuses on segment storage reliability, compaction and recovery. Team members work together when an index format change improves cost but changes ranking behavior on particular query groups. The team maintains explicit interfaces between ingestion, the index build pipeline and serving. Engineers rotate through operational review and use small deployments to investigate unexpected results before broader rollout. Developer Productivity, where Maya Chen works, supports build and deployment tooling across these groups. The November directory reflects current assignments; archived articles remain available because they describe the systems as they existed at publication.

documents.title: Linden engineering talks November 2026
documents.text: Talks: Priya Iyer, Query slices and retrieval evaluation; Jordan Wells, Segment compaction and reliable indexing. Both are Retrieval Infrastructure engineers. Links: /talk-priya and /talk-jordan.

documents.title: Priya Iyer: Query slices and retrieval evaluation
documents.text: Priya Iyer, Retrieval Infrastructure: Query slices and retrieval evaluation. A single aggregate quality score can hide regressions affecting uncommon queries. This talk follows an index change through a fixed evaluation set, comparing recall and ranking quality by query length, language and document freshness. Priya describes why the team keeps both a broad reference set and narrower regression cases. Engineers inspect disagreements between the sets instead of treating an improved average as a complete release decision. The examples compare reranked results against earlier retrieval stages and discuss the time cost of evaluating many candidates. A final section covers reproducibility: storing the index version, query set version and configuration alongside a result so another engineer can investigate it. Questions from the audience address noisy labels, stale documents and balancing evaluation speed against confidence. Speaker profile: https://linden.example.test/people/priya-iyer.

documents.title: Jordan Wells: Segment compaction and reliable indexing
documents.text: Jordan Wells, Retrieval Infrastructure: Segment compaction and reliable indexing. Many small immutable segments make incremental updates easy, but increase metadata overhead and read amplification. Compaction trades temporary write and disk usage for simpler reads. Jordan follows a versioned index through a merge, a worker restart and recovery. Readers must keep a consistent view while the new version is prepared, and old objects cannot be removed until active readers no longer need them. The talk describes validation checks before publishing a segment manifest, metrics for abandoned merge work and the value of testing interrupted writes. The examples emphasize failure recovery and correctness before tuning throughput. Audience questions compare whole-segment rewrites with incremental changes and ask how teams decide when background compaction is consuming too much capacity. Speaker profile: https://linden.example.test/people/jordan-wells.
